_about: Why each default is what it is, and on which data it was checked. Keyed by module.method; `validated_on` names the bundled data or the test that exercised the method; `params` holds one sentence per parameter. Read by the catalog loader into Parameter.rationale / Parameter.validated_on; printed by pl.describe(); rendered on the docs pages. Keep every parameter covered: tests/test_catalog.py fails otherwise.

point_cloud_processing.voxel_downsample.validated_on: Stanford bunny (0.15 m, examples/poisson_reconstruction_bunny), KITTI sweeps (metres, examples/kitti_lidar_ground_and_objects); generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.voxel_size: 0.02 in file units: on a metre-scale object or room it keeps one point per 2 cm, enough for registration features and clustering; set it to 2-5x the point spacing of your scanner (0.5 mm for CBCT, 0.1 m for outdoor LiDAR), because the value is absolute, not relative to the object.

point_cloud_processing.statistical_outli.validated_on: Stanford bunny with 0.5 % Gaussian noise (examples/poisson_reconstruction_bunny, examples/icp_registration_bunny); generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.nb_neighbors: 20 neighbours give a stable mean distance per point on scans of 10k-1M points; fewer makes the estimate noisy, more blurs the boundary between surface and stray points.
params.std_ratio: 2.0 removes points whose mean neighbour distance is beyond two standard deviations: on scanner noise this drops the flying pixels and keeps thin structures; lower to 1.0 on very noisy depth-camera data, raise to 3.0 on clean CAD-derived clouds.
params.print_progress: Off: the progress bar writes to the terminal and is useless in a pipeline or an agent run.

params.radius: 0.05 in file units: a point with fewer than min_neighbors within 5 cm is isolated on a metre-scale scan; scale with the point spacing (about 10x the spacing).
params.min_neighbors: 5 is low enough to keep edges and thin parts, where neighbourhoods are naturally sparse, while isolated speckle has 0-2 neighbours.

params.iterations: 1 iteration quadruples the triangle count; two or more are rarely needed before smoothing and make files large quickly.

mesh_processing.simplification.validated_on: Stanford bunny (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh uses the PyVista decimation instead); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.target_triangles: 5 000 triangles is the size at which an organ or part surface still looks right on screen and loads instantly in a viewer; raise it for metrology.
params.maximum_error: Unbounded (1e30) matches Open3D's behaviour: the decimation stops at the triangle budget, not at an error threshold, so the result is predictable in size.
params.boundary_weight: 1.0 treats boundary edges like interior ones; raise it on open meshes (scans with holes) so the boundary does not shrink.

mesh_processing.mesh_to_pcd_uniform.validated_on: Stanford bunny (examples/points_to_gaussians_bunny); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.num_points: 5 000 points keep registration and clustering fast while covering a surface; the examples use 20 000-50 000 for visual density.
params.use_triangle_normal: Off: interpolated vertex normals are smoother on organic surfaces; turn on for CAD meshes with flat faces.
params.seed: -1 (non-deterministic) is Open3D's default; set a seed when a result must be reproducible, as the examples do.

mesh_processing.mesh_to_pcd_poisson_disk.validated_on: Stanford bunny (examples/poisson_reconstruction_bunny, examples/icp_registration_bunny); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.num_points: 5 000 is the approximate count after elimination: Poisson-disk sampling gives evenly spaced points, which is what registration features and PointNet training want.
params.init_factor: 5x oversampling before elimination is Open3D's recommendation: enough candidates for an even blue-noise distribution without a long elimination pass.
params.use_triangle_normal: Off: interpolated normals; on for flat-faced CAD meshes.
params.seed: -1 is non-deterministic; the examples pass seed=1 for reproducible figures.

params.voxel_size: 0.01 in file units gives a 100-voxel grid across a unit-sized object: coarse enough to run in a second, fine enough to see shape; the range (0.002-0.05) assumes objects around a metre, so scale it for millimetre data.
Same grid as voxelization so the two can be compared on the same object.
params.erosion_iterations: 1 iteration removes one voxel layer: the thinnest shell, which is what you want to strip surface noise without eating thin parts.
params.erosion_connectivity: 1 (faces only) is the most conservative structuring element: each iteration removes the least material.
params.iso_level: 0.5 is the half-occupancy surface of a binary grid: the boundary between inside and outside voxels.
params.padding_voxels: 5 voxels of margin keep marching cubes from clipping the surface at the grid border.

params.voxel_size: 0.01 in file units for a 100-voxel grid on a unit object; the SDF cost grows with the cube of the resolution.
params.padding: 5 voxels of margin so the zero level set is closed inside the grid.
params.level: 0.0 is the surface itself (zero signed distance); offset it to inflate or shrink the mesh.
params.mc_step_size: 1 samples every voxel; a larger step is a quick coarse preview.
params.mc_method: Lewiner marching cubes resolves the ambiguous cases that the original Lorensen tables get wrong on thin structures.
params.mc_gradient_direction: descent orients normals so that the inside is negative distance, which is the convention of the SDF grid.
params.mc_allow_degenerate: On, matching scikit-image: degenerate triangles are removed later by the mesh cleaning step rather than by rejecting the surface.

params.voxel_size: Same grid as compute_sdf for comparable results.
params.padding: 5 voxels of margin around the bounding box.
params.level: 0.5 is the half-occupancy boundary of a binary occupancy grid.
params.mc_gradient_direction: descent keeps normals pointing outward for occupancy grids.

params.resolution: 32 voxels per axis (32 768 cells) renders in a second and still shows the shape of the field; it is a visualisation, not the SDF you compute with.
params.min_clamp: -0.1 clamps the interior so colours stay readable near the surface instead of saturating at the object centre.
params.max_clamp: 0.1 clamps the exterior for the same reason.
params.padding_factor: 15 % of the extent as margin shows the field decaying outside the object.
params.colormap: coolwarm is diverging around zero, which is what a signed field needs: blue inside, red outside.

point_cloud_reconstruction.poisson.validated_on: Stanford bunny sampled to 20 000 points (examples/poisson_reconstruction_bunny); ultrasound and CBCT reconstructions in the atlas-label-transfer and pointnet-segmentation skills; generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.depth: 9 gives 512 cells across the bounding cube: on 20k-200k point scans it recovers organ- and part-level detail without fitting the noise; 8 is Open3D's default and blurs small features, 10-11 need hundreds of thousands of points.
params.scale: 1.1 is the Kazhdan reference setting: the reconstruction cube is 10 % larger than the samples' bounding cube so the surface can close outside the data.
params.width: 0 means depth drives the resolution; set a width in file units when you know the target cell size (e.g. 1 mm).
params.linear_fit: Off: the default iso-vertex placement is smoother; linear fit is faster and slightly blockier.
params.density_quantile: 0.01 removes the 1 % of vertices with the least sample support: that is where Poisson balloons over holes and partial views, so the output is a clean, density-trimmed surface rather than a bubble; raise to 0.05-0.1 on very partial scans.
params.normal_radius: 0.1 in file units for normal estimation when the cloud has none; about 5-10x the point spacing on metre-scale data, scale it for millimetre scans.
params.normal_max_nn: 30 neighbours is enough for a stable covariance; more smooths sharp edges.
params.normal_orient_k: 15 neighbours for consistent orientation: Poisson needs normals pointing the same way, and a small k keeps the propagation local on thin parts.

params.joggle_inputs: Off: exact hull; turn on only when QHull fails on coplanar or duplicated points.

params.alpha: 0.03 in file units is a tight fit on metre-scale objects with centimetre point spacing; alpha must be larger than the largest gap you want bridged and smaller than the smallest concavity you want kept.

params.radius_factor: 2x the average point spacing is the smallest ball that rolls over a sampled surface without falling through; the multi-scale set (1x, 2x, 4x) then fills the larger gaps.
params.radii_multipliers: 1,2,4 is the classic multi-scale schedule: small balls first for detail, larger ones to bridge sparse regions.
params.normal_radius: 0.1 in file units for normal estimation when the cloud has none.
params.normal_orient_k: 15 for consistent orientation; ball pivoting needs oriented normals.

registration.ransac_global.validated_on: Stanford bunny, 35 deg / 70 % overlap / 0.5 % noise (examples/icp_registration_bunny: 0.14 deg residual after ICP); ultrasound and CBCT reconstructions in the atlas-label-transfer skill (0.06 deg pose error on the bunny atlas); Open3D indoor fragments

params.voxel_size: 0.5 is a placeholder for the platform UI; 0 (auto) is what the one-call API passes: 1.3 % of the bounding-box diagonal, so the feature scale follows the object instead of a fixed number that is wrong for both a 15 cm part and a 15 m facade.
params.normal_radius_factor: 2x the voxel: normals need a neighbourhood a little larger than the downsampling cell to be stable but local.
params.normal_max_nn: 30 neighbours cap the normal estimation cost on dense clouds.
params.fpfh_radius_factor: 5x the voxel is the Open3D-recommended FPFH support: large enough for a descriptive 33-bin histogram, small enough to stay local on partial scans.
params.distance_threshold_factor: 1.5x the voxel: a correspondence within one and a half cells counts as an inlier; tighter rejects true matches on noisy scans, looser lets outliers vote.
params.mutual_filter: On: both directions of the feature match must agree, which removes most false correspondences before RANSAC and is the single setting that most improves success on symmetric parts.
params.ransac_with_scaling: Off: rigid scans share a scale; turn on only for photogrammetry against a scanner.
params.ransac_n: 3 correspondences is the minimum for a rigid transform; 4 helps on symmetric objects at the cost of more iterations.
params.edge_length_threshold: 0.9: the pairwise distances of the sampled correspondences must agree within 10 %, which prunes wrong triplets before the expensive inlier count.
params.ransac_max_iteration: 100 000 iterations with the early-stop confidence below converge in seconds on 20k-point clouds.
params.ransac_confidence: 0.999 stops once the best model is that likely to be the true one.

registration.icp_refinement.validated_on: Stanford bunny (examples/icp_registration_bunny); Open3D indoor fragments; generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.voxel_size: 0 (auto) picks 1.3 % of the bounding-box diagonal; the explicit 0.5 is the platform UI placeholder.
params.max_iterations: 2 000 is a ceiling, not a target: point-to-plane ICP stops on the relative thresholds long before.
params.icp_estimation_method: point_to_plane converges in far fewer iterations and slides along surfaces instead of fighting them; point-to-point is the automatic fallback when normals cannot be estimated (sparse LiDAR).
params.relative_fitness: 1e-6: stop when the inlier fraction no longer changes.
params.relative_rmse: 1e-6: stop when the inlier RMSE no longer changes.
params.icp_threshold_factor: 1.5x the voxel on the downsampled pass: generous so the first ICP pass can pull a coarse RANSAC pose in.
params.refine_threshold_factor: 0.4x the voxel on the full-resolution pass: tight so the last iterations are not pulled by points without a true counterpart (the 30 % non-overlap of a partial scan).
params.normal_max_nn: 30 neighbours cap the normal-estimation cost on dense clouds while keeping the covariance stable.
params.fpfh_radius_factor: 5x the voxel for the RANSAC pre-pass features.
params.fpfh_max_nn: 100 neighbours bound the FPFH histogram cost; the radius, not the count, sets the feature scale.
params.ransac_distance_factor: 1.5x the voxel for the pre-pass inlier distance.
params.ransac_with_scaling: Off: two rigid scans share a scale; estimating one only makes sense for photogrammetry against a scanner.
params.ransac_n: 3 correspondences is the minimum that determines a rigid transform, which keeps the inlier probability per draw highest.
params.ransac_seed_fitness: 0.3: below this pre-pass fitness the features were not informative and ICP starts from the centre-of-mass alignment instead of a wrong pose.

registration.ransac_icp_pipeline.validated_on: Stanford bunny, 35 deg / 70 % overlap / 0.5 % noise: 0.14 deg residual, inlier RMSE 0.9 mm against a 1.4 mm noise floor (examples/icp_registration_bunny); bunny atlas transfer 99.4 % label agreement (examples/atlas_label_transfer_bunny); Open3D indoor fragments

params.voxel_size: 0 (auto) = 1.3 % of the bounding-box diagonal: every other distance is a multiple of it, so one number adapts the whole pipeline to a 15 cm part or a 15 m facade; the explicit 0.5 is the platform UI placeholder.
params.rotation_degrees: 45 degrees is used only in demo mode (no moving cloud): a synthetic rotation large enough to defeat plain ICP so the global stage is visibly needed.
params.normal_radius_factor: 2x the voxel for stable but local normals.
params.normal_max_nn: 30 neighbours cap the normal-estimation cost on dense clouds while keeping the covariance stable.
params.fpfh_radius_factor: 5x the voxel: the Open3D-recommended FPFH support.
params.fpfh_max_nn: 100 neighbours bound the FPFH histogram cost; the radius, not the count, sets the feature scale.
params.distance_threshold_factor: 1.5x the voxel for RANSAC inliers: tolerant to scanner noise, still rejects outliers.
params.mutual_filter: On: mutual nearest-neighbour matching is the setting that most reduces false correspondences on symmetric or repetitive parts.
params.ransac_with_scaling: Off: two rigid scans share a scale; estimating one only makes sense for photogrammetry against a scanner.
params.ransac_n: 3 correspondences, the minimum for a rigid transform.
params.edge_length_threshold: 0.9: prune triplets whose pairwise distances disagree by more than 10 %.
params.icp_threshold_factor: 0.4x the voxel for the final ICP: tight, so the refinement is driven by true overlap and not by the partial-view points that have no counterpart.
params.icp_estimation_method: point_to_plane: faster convergence and no sliding across flat regions compared with point-to-point; point-to-point is the automatic fallback without normals.
params.icp_max_iteration: 30 iterations after a good global pose is enough; the relative thresholds usually stop it earlier.

deformable_registration.cpd_deformable.validated_on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py; the point-cloud-registration skill documents its use after a rigid stage

params.max_iterations: 100 EM iterations: CPD converges in 30-80 on organ-sized clouds; the tolerance below usually stops it first.
params.tolerance: 1e-3 relative change of the objective: tighter costs iterations without visible change in the displacement field.
params.beta: 100 is pycpd's default Gaussian kernel width in file units, i.e. a very smooth, almost global deformation for unit-scale clouds; lower it to about the size of the structures you expect to move independently (10-20 mm for organs).
params.lambda_val: 2.0 regularisation weight: the pycpd default, balancing fit against smoothness; raise it when the field folds.
params.w: 0 assumes no outliers; set 0.1-0.3 when the fixed cloud has clutter the moving cloud should not reach.
params.low_rank: Off below about 10k points; on above, where the full kernel matrix no longer fits in memory.
params.num_eig: 100 eigenvectors keep the low-rank approximation close to the full kernel at a fraction of the cost.

params.displacement: 0.02 in file units: a visible but plausible dent on a unit-scale object, used to synthesise test cases for non-rigid registration.
params.radius: 0.1 in file units: the dent spans 10 % of a unit object.
params.sigma_factor: 0.5: the Gaussian falls to about 13 % at the radius, so the dent fades smoothly instead of leaving a crease.

point_cloud_segmentation.ransac_plane.validated_on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py; the same RANSAC plane model runs on KITTI in lidar_scene_detection

params.distance_threshold: 0.01 in file units: one centimetre on metre-scale indoor scans, which is the depth-camera noise level; use 0.2-0.3 m for outdoor LiDAR ground.
params.num_iterations: 1 000 iterations find the dominant plane with probability above 0.99 when it holds at least 20 % of the points.
params.ransac_n: 3 points define a plane; the minimum keeps the inlier probability per draw highest.
params.probability: 0.99999999 lets Open3D stop early once the best plane is almost certainly found, so the 1 000 iterations are a ceiling.

point_cloud_segmentation.dbscan_clusteri.validated_on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py; KITTI sweeps through lidar_scene_detection.object_clustering

params.eps: 0.02 in file units: two centimetres joins points of the same object on indoor depth scans; use 0.5 m outdoors (see object_clustering).
params.min_points: 10 points keep speckle out of the cluster list while small objects (a cup, a hand) still form one.

params.colormap: 0 (jet) is what stereo and depth tooling has used for decades, so the colours are readable at a glance; the others are perceptually uniform alternatives.

params.min_depth: Dropping the nearest 10 % removes the lens-edge and occlusion artefacts stereo matching produces close to the camera.
params.max_depth: Dropping the farthest 10 % removes the sky and the far-range noise where disparity is below one pixel.

lidar_scene_detection.height_colorizatio.validated_on: KITTI sweeps (examples/kitti_lidar_ground_and_objects); generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.colormap: 0 (height gradient) maps the sensor z axis directly to colour, which is how LiDAR engineers read a sweep.

lidar_scene_detection.ground_removal.validated_on: KITTI Velodyne HDL-64E sweeps, sensor frame, metres (examples/kitti_lidar_ground_and_objects)

params.distance_threshold: 0.3 m: a road is not flat over a 100 m sweep (camber, slope, curb), so a 30 cm band keeps the whole surface as ground while a car's lowest points (sills at 0.4-0.5 m) stay out; lower to 0.1 m for indoor floors.
params.num_iterations: 1 000 iterations are plenty when the ground holds 30-50 % of a sweep's points.

lidar_scene_detection.object_clustering.validated_on: KITTI sweeps: 35 476 points clustered into cars, poles, walls after ground removal (examples/kitti_lidar_ground_and_objects)

params.ground_threshold: 0.3 m, as in ground_removal: the band that follows a real road's camber and slope.
params.cluster_eps: 0.5 m: the HDL-64E spacing between rings reaches 0.3-0.5 m at 30 m, so a smaller epsilon splits one car into ring-stripes; a larger one merges parked cars.
params.min_cluster_points: 10 points keep ring fragments and speckle out while a pedestrian at 20 m (about 15-30 points) still clusters.

lidar_camera_fusion.intensity_colorizati.validated_on: KITTI sweeps carry reflectance in the fourth column (manifest layout); generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.colormap: 0 (jet) for reflectance: lane paint and plates saturate to red, asphalt stays blue, which is what people look for in an intensity view.

params.x_range: Keep the central 50 % along x: the near field in front of and behind the sensor, where the camera overlap is.
params.y_range: Keep the central 50 % along y: the lane and its neighbours.
params.z_range: Keep 80 % along z: drops only the extreme returns (tree tops, below-ground reflections).

params.levels: 3 levels (base, 2x, 4x) are what multi-scale registration and visualisation consume.
params.base_voxel_size: 0.01 in file units at the finest level, matching voxel_downsample's default.
params.voxel_growth_factor: 2x per level: the standard octave pyramid.

features_extraction.normal_estimation.validated_on: Stanford bunny through the registration pipeline; generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.radius: 0.05 in file units: about 5x the spacing of a centimetre-resolution scan; the covariance needs 10-30 points inside the radius.
params.max_nn: 30 neighbours cap the cost and keep normals local at edges.
params.fast_normal_computation: On: Open3D's closed-form eigen solver is accurate to visual precision and several times faster than the iterative one.
params.orient_k: 0 lets the script choose min(max_nn, 15) for the orientation propagation: small enough to stay consistent across thin parts.

features_extraction.fpfh_features.validated_on: Stanford bunny and Open3D fragments through registration.ransac_global; generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.voxel_size: 0.005 in file units (5 mm on a metre object) keeps enough points for descriptive histograms; the registration pipeline derives it from the bounding box instead.
params.normal_max_nn: 30 neighbours cap the normal-estimation cost on dense clouds while keeping the covariance stable.
params.feature_radius_factor: 5x the voxel: the Open3D-recommended FPFH support.

params.radius: 0.05 in file units for the covariance neighbourhood, as for normals.
params.max_nn: 30 neighbours cap the cost and keep the estimate local at edges.
params.normalize_percentile: Colour scale capped at the 99th percentile so a few extreme points (edges, noise) do not flatten the map.

params.obstacle_radius: 0.5 in file units: a sphere half the size of a unit object, the demo obstacle.
params.penetration_ratio: 0.3: the obstacle is placed so that 30 % of its radius overlaps the part, enough to show a clear collision patch.
params.num_samples: 50 000 surface samples give a dense signed-distance map on the part in under a second.
params.obstacle_resolution: 50 tessellation steps make the sphere smooth enough that its SDF has no facet artefacts.
params.obstacle_viz_points: 5 000 points draw the obstacle without hiding the part.
params.colormap: coolwarm is diverging around zero distance: red inside the obstacle, blue outside.

params.obstacle_radius: 0.5 in file units, the demo obstacle.
params.overlap_distance: 0.15 in file units: the obstacle overlaps the part by 15 % of a unit object.
params.obstacle_resolution: 50 tessellation steps make the sphere smooth enough that its SDF has no facet artefacts.
params.colormap: hot maps zero depth to black and the deepest penetration to white.

pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_decimate.validated_on: MSD hippocampus surfaces (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh, decimate 0.5); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.target_reduction: 0.5 halves the triangle count: on marching-cubes output (one triangle per voxel face) that removes the redundant co-planar triangles with no visible change.
params.volume_preservation: Off: VTK's default; on when the mesh is used for volume measurements (organs), since plain quadric decimation shrinks convex shapes slightly.
params.attribute_error: Off: ignore scalar fields in the error metric; on when a label or curvature field must survive decimation.
params.normals: Off: do not penalise normal deviation; on for CAD meshes with sharp edges.
params.boundary_constraints: Off: VTK's current boundary handling; the legacy weighting is for reproducing old results.

params.n_subdivisions: 1 iteration quadruples the triangle count, which is as much as a smoothing or sampling step ever needs.
params.algorithm: linear keeps the surface exactly where it is and only adds vertices; butterfly and loop also smooth, which changes the geometry.

pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_smooth_laplac.validated_on: MSD hippocampus surfaces (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.n_iterations: 20 iterations remove the voxel staircase of a marching-cubes surface; more than 50 visibly shrinks small structures.
params.relaxation_factor: 0.01 is VTK's default step: small steps over 20 iterations move vertices by less than a voxel in total.
params.convergence: 0 disables early stop so the iteration count is the only knob.
params.edge_angle: 15 degrees is VTK's edge-feature threshold when feature smoothing is on.
params.feature_angle: 45 degrees is VTK's sharp-feature threshold when feature smoothing is on.
params.boundary_smoothing: On: boundary vertices of open surfaces move too, otherwise the rim stays jagged.
params.feature_smoothing: Off: organic surfaces have no sharp features to preserve; on for CAD parts.

pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_smooth_taubin.validated_on: MSD hippocampus surfaces: the default mesh.smooth() (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.n_iterations: 20 iterations remove the voxel staircase; Taubin's pass band keeps the volume, so the count can be higher than for Laplacian smoothing without shrinkage.
params.pass_band: 0.1 is VTK's default: frequencies above it are attenuated (staircase), below it kept (anatomy); lower it for a smoother result.
params.boundary_smoothing: On so open rims are smoothed too.
params.non_manifold_smoothing: Off: non-manifold vertices (two sheets touching) are left in place to avoid tearing.
params.normalize_coordinates: Off: VTK's default; on for coordinates with very large magnitudes (UTM metres) to keep the filter numerically stable.

pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_clean.validated_on: every Mesh.clean() in the examples; generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.tolerance: 0 merges exact duplicates only: safe on any mesh; a positive tolerance welds nearby vertices and can close scan seams.
params.point_merging: On: duplicate vertices from STL files and marching cubes are merged.
params.absolute: On: the tolerance is in file units, not a fraction of the bounding box, so it means the same thing on every mesh.
params.lines_to_points: On: zero-length lines become points instead of invalid cells.

params.hole_size: 100 in file units is the largest hole (by boundary radius) that is filled: scan holes, not the open bottom of a bust.

params.consistency: 1: make neighbouring faces agree, which STL files from scanners often do not.
params.cell_normals: On: per-face normals for rendering and sampling.
params.point_normals: On: per-vertex normals for smooth shading and registration.
params.split_vertices: Off: splitting duplicates vertices along sharp edges and breaks the connectivity other steps rely on.
params.auto_orient_normals: Off: it assumes a closed manifold and inverts open scans.
params.non_manifold_traversal: On: orientation does not propagate across non-manifold edges, where it would flip.
params.feature_angle: 30 degrees when split_vertices is on, VTK's default.

pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_extract_surfa.validated_on: every Volume.to_mesh() result goes through surface extraction (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.pass_pointid: On: keep the original point ids so results can be mapped back to the volume.
params.pass_cellid: On: keep the original cell ids for the same reason.
params.nonlinear_subdivision: 1 matches VTK's default for higher-order cells; the grids here are linear.

params.lower: 0 and upper 1 select a normalised scalar range; set them to your field's units (HU, reflectance).
params.scalars: Empty uses the active scalar array, which is what a freshly loaded file has.
params.invert: Off: keep what is inside the range.
params.continuous: Off: a cell is kept on its own scalar, not on the range it spans.
params.preference: cell: VTK's default when both point and cell scalars exist.
params.all_scalars: Off: a cell is kept if any of its points pass, which keeps boundaries intact.
params.component_mode: all: every component of a vector scalar must pass.
params.component: 0: the first component when component_mode is component.

params.origin_x: 0: the plane passes through the origin by default; set it to a point on the cut you want.
params.normal_x: 1: cut perpendicular to x by default.
params.invert: On keeps the side the normal points away from, VTK's convention for clip.
params.crinkle: Off: cells crossed by the plane are cut, giving a flat face; on keeps them whole, which preserves the original cells.

params.x_min: -0.5 to 0.5 is a unit box around the origin, the placeholder for normalised data; set the box in file units.
params.invert: Off: keep the inside of the box.
params.merge_points: On: coincident points created by the clip are merged.

params.fraction: 0.5 halves a cloud, the usual first step before an interactive look at a multi-million-point scan.
params.seed: -1 is non-deterministic, matching the original script; set a seed for reproducible figures.
params.adjacent_cells: On: cells touching a selected point are kept so meshes stay connected.

params.lower: 0 with upper 1 is a normalised range placeholder.

pyvista_volume_processing.pv_contour.validated_on: MSD and RIRE volumes through Volume.to_mesh (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh, examples/spleen_ct_threshold_segmentation); generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.n_contours: 5 evenly spaced iso-levels show the structure of an unknown field; a label map or a known threshold uses one level through Volume.to_mesh.
params.scalars: Empty uses the active scalars (the image intensity).
params.compute_normals: Off: normals are recomputed later by the mesh steps that need them.
params.compute_gradients: Off: not needed for a surface.
params.compute_scalars: On: the contoured value is kept on the surface for colouring.
params.method: contour is VTK's generic filter; marching_cubes and flying_edges are faster on image data and give the same surface.
params.preference: point: image intensities are point data.

pyvista_volume_processing.pv_slice.validated_on: RIRE and MSD volumes (README demo slices); generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.normal_x: 1: an x-normal (sagittal in LPS) slice by default.
params.generate_triangles: Off: the slice stays a polygon mesh of quads.

pyvista_volume_processing.pv_slice_ortho.validated_on: MSD hippocampus MRI (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.x: 0 means the centre of the volume.
params.generate_triangles: Off: the slice stays a polygon mesh of quads, which renders and saves smaller.
params.contour: Off: no contour edges are generated on the slice.

params.lower: 0 with upper 1 is a normalised placeholder; use Hounsfield units on CT.
params.invert: Off: keep the inside of the range.
params.continuous: Off: a cell is kept on its own scalar value, not on the range it spans.
params.all_scalars: Off: a cell is kept if any of its points pass, which keeps boundaries intact.

params.extent: Empty keeps the whole dataset; a six-number extent crops in index space.

params.cell_type: tetrahedral is the cell type of simulation meshes (VTU), the usual reason to extract by type.

params.curvature_type: mean curvature is the one that reads as 'bumps and dents' on an organ or a part; Gaussian separates saddles, maximum/minimum are the principal curvatures.

params.scale_factor: 0.01 in file units draws normal arrows of 1 % of a unit object, visible without hiding the surface.
params.vector_name: Normals is the array every mesh has after compute_normals.
params.scale: Off: all arrows the same length, so direction is what you see.
params.tolerance: -1 lets PyVista choose the glyph merge tolerance.
params.absolute: Off: the tolerance is a fraction of the bounding box.
params.clamping: Off: no scaling range clamp since scale is off.

params.vector_name: Normals is the array every mesh has.

params.scalars: Empty takes the first available array.

params.feature_angle: 30 degrees is VTK's default dihedral threshold: it catches machined edges and misses the facets of a smooth organ.
params.boundary_edges: true: open boundaries are what you look for on a scan with holes.
params.non_manifold_edges: true: non-manifold edges are the defects to fix before printing or simulation.
params.manifold_edges: false: regular edges would be every edge of the mesh.
params.clear_data: Off: keep the scalar arrays on the edges.

simpleitk_registration.rigid.validated_on: RIRE CT / MR-T1 brain pair: 0.65 x 0.65 x 4 mm CT vs 1.25 x 1.25 x 4 mm MR, 40 mm initial offset, registered in 8.8 s (examples/register_ct_mr_rire, the README demo); the multimodal-rigid-registration skill reports 3.9 deg / 1 mm-class agreement with the RIRE truth

params.learning_rate: 1.0 with optimizer scales from physical shift: each step moves the image by about one unit of the scaled parameters, fast on the coarse levels and still stable because the scales normalise rotations and translations.
params.num_iterations: 100 per level: Mattes MI on 1 % sampling plateaus within 50-80 iterations on head and abdomen volumes; the convergence window stops it earlier.
params.sampling_percentage: 1 % of the voxels is enough for the MI estimate on 256^3 volumes and makes each iteration cheap; raise to 5-15 % on small fields of view or very noisy images.
params.initializer: GEOMETRY aligns the geometric centres of the two volumes, which works when both scans cover the same anatomy; MOMENTS (intensity centre of mass) is better when one field of view is much larger than the other.
params.metric: Mattes mutual information is the only one of the four that works across modalities (CT vs MR): it assumes a statistical dependence, not a linear intensity relation.
params.number_of_histogram_bins: 50 bins: 32-64 is the sweet spot for the Parzen-window joint histogram, fewer is blurry, more is noisy.
params.sampling_strategy: RANDOM adds a little stochasticity that helps the optimizer leave shallow local minima; REGULAR aliases with voxel grids.
params.interpolator: LINEAR during optimisation is the standard trade-off; B-spline is slower and only pays off for the final resampling.
params.convergence_minimum_value: 1e-6 on the metric change over the window.
params.convergence_window_size: 10 iterations smooth the stochastic metric before the convergence test.
params.shrink_factors: 4,2,1: three resolution levels give the capture range to recover a 40 mm offset at the coarse level and sub-voxel precision at the fine one.
params.smoothing_sigmas: 2,1,0 mm match the shrink factors so each level sees a properly band-limited image.
params.smoothing_sigmas_in_physical_units: On: sigmas in millimetres so anisotropic voxels (4 mm slices) are smoothed consistently.
params.optimizer_scales_from_physical_shift: On: rotations in radians and translations in millimetres have different sensitivities; the physical-shift scales equalise them, which is the single setting that makes a fixed learning rate work across datasets.

simpleitk_registration.advanced_rigid.validated_on: RIRE CT / MR pair with the exhaustive rotation pre-search (multimodal-rigid-registration skill); generated volumes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.learning_rate: 0.2 is lower than the plain rigid method because the exhaustive phase already lands near the optimum; smaller steps then avoid overshooting.
params.num_iterations: 200 per stage: the second stage starts close and the window stops it early.
params.sampling_percentage: 15 % of the voxels: the exhaustive search compares many poses and needs a less noisy metric than gradient descent does.
params.exhaustive_steps_per_axis: 12 steps per axis over the rotation range sample every 15 degrees, enough to land inside the capture range of the gradient stage.
params.number_of_histogram_bins: 50 bins: 32-64 is the sweet spot for the Parzen-window joint histogram, fewer is blurry, more is noisy.
params.sampling_strategy: RANDOM sampling adds a little stochasticity that helps the optimizer leave shallow local minima; REGULAR aliases with voxel grids.
params.interpolator: LINEAR interpolation during optimisation is the standard trade-off between speed and smoothness of the metric.
params.convergence_minimum_value: 1e-6 on the metric change over the window stops the optimizer once improvements are below noise.
params.convergence_window_size: 10 iterations smooth the stochastic metric before the convergence test.
params.shrink_factors: 4,2,1: three resolution levels give the capture range for large offsets at the coarse level and sub-voxel precision at the fine one.
params.smoothing_sigmas: 2,1,0 mm match the shrink factors so each level sees a properly band-limited image.
params.smoothing_sigmas_in_physical_units: On: sigmas in millimetres so anisotropic voxels (4 mm slices) are smoothed consistently.
params.optimizer_scales_from_physical_shift: On: rotations in radians and translations in millimetres have different sensitivities; physical-shift scales equalise them so one learning rate works across datasets.

simpleitk_registration.affine.validated_on: generated volumes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py; same stack as rigid, which ran on the RIRE pair

params.learning_rate: 1.0 with physical-shift scales, as for rigid.
params.sampling_percentage: 1 % of the voxels is enough for the mutual-information estimate on 256^3 volumes and keeps each iteration cheap.
params.initializer: GEOMETRY aligns the geometric centres before the first iteration; MOMENTS (intensity centre of mass) when one field of view is much larger than the other.
params.metric: Mattes MI for cross-modality; mean squares is faster for same-modality follow-ups.
params.number_of_histogram_bins: 50 bins: 32-64 is the sweet spot for the Parzen-window joint histogram, fewer is blurry, more is noisy.
params.sampling_strategy: RANDOM sampling adds a little stochasticity that helps the optimizer leave shallow local minima; REGULAR aliases with voxel grids.
params.interpolator: LINEAR interpolation during optimisation is the standard trade-off between speed and smoothness of the metric.
params.convergence_minimum_value: 1e-6 on the metric change over the window stops the optimizer once improvements are below noise.
params.convergence_window_size: 10 iterations smooth the stochastic metric before the convergence test.
params.shrink_factors: 4,2,1: three resolution levels give the capture range for large offsets at the coarse level and sub-voxel precision at the fine one.
params.smoothing_sigmas: 2,1,0 mm match the shrink factors so each level sees a properly band-limited image.
params.smoothing_sigmas_in_physical_units: On: sigmas in millimetres so anisotropic voxels (4 mm slices) are smoothed consistently.
params.optimizer_scales_from_physical_shift: On: the 12 affine parameters mix scale, shear and translation, so scale normalisation matters even more than for rigid.

simpleitk_registration.bspline.validated_on: POPI 4D-CT breathing phases (medical-volumes skill); generated volumes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.grid_spacing: 50 mm control-point spacing captures organ-scale motion (breathing, bowel) without fitting noise; 20-30 mm for finer local deformation.
params.num_iterations: 100 LBFGSB iterations: the deformable metric improves quickly then flattens.
params.mesh_coarsening_factor: 4 starts the multi-resolution schedule with a coarser control mesh so large motion is recovered first.
params.sampling_percentage: 1 % of the voxels for the metric.
params.interpolator: LINEAR interpolation during optimisation is the standard trade-off between speed and smoothness of the metric.
params.max_number_of_corrections: 5 stored corrections is the LBFGSB default memory.
params.scale_factors: 1,2,4 refine the control mesh across three levels.

simpleitk_registration.demons.validated_on: generated volumes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py; same-modality use only (the metric is intensity difference)

params.num_iterations: 20 demons iterations are enough for small same-modality deformations; the method is for follow-up scans, not CT-to-MR.
params.standard_deviations: 2.0 voxels of Gaussian smoothing of the displacement field keep it regular (no folding) at the cost of fine detail.
params.smooth_displacement_field: On: smoothing the total field each iteration is what keeps demons from producing a torn deformation.

params.lower_threshold: 50 intensity units: below that, differences are noise and interpolation.
params.upper_threshold: 400: above that, differences are bone or air boundaries that any residual misalignment produces; the band in between highlights soft-tissue change.

simpleitk_segmentation.otsu_threshold.validated_on: MSD spleen CT through Volume.segment() (examples/spleen_ct_threshold_segmentation uses the manual window); generated volumes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.number_of_histogram_bins: 128 bins resolve the bimodal histogram of CT (air/tissue) or MR (background/foreground) without the noise of 512.
params.inside_value: 1: the foreground label, so the result is a LabelMap with label 1.
params.outside_value: 0 is the background label, so the result is a label map with a single foreground label.

simpleitk_segmentation.manual_threshold.validated_on: MSD spleen CT, 30-200 HU soft-tissue window (examples/spleen_ct_threshold_segmentation); generated volumes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.lower: 100 HU is the placeholder bone/contrast threshold on CT; Volume.segment(lower, upper) takes the window you mean (30-200 HU soft tissue, 300+ bone).
params.upper: 1000 HU caps the window below metal and dense bone.
params.outside_value: 0 is the background label, so the result is a label map with a single foreground label.

simpleitk_segmentation.connected_compone.validated_on: MSD spleen CT after thresholding (examples/spleen_ct_threshold_segmentation, min_size 1000); generated volumes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

params.threshold: 100 intensity units binarises before labelling; on a LabelMap input use 0.5.
params.min_size: 15 voxels removes speckle components; raise to the hundreds or thousands to keep only organs.
params.upper_threshold: 255 is the upper bound for 8-bit inputs; raise it for HU.
params.fully_connected: Off (6-connectivity): diagonal-only contacts do not join two structures, which keeps touching organs apart.
params.outside_value: 0 is the background label, so the result is a label map with a single foreground label.

params.threshold: 100 intensity units for the initial binarisation.
params.seed_radius: 10 mm: markers are placed where the distance map exceeds this radius, so only objects at least 2 cm across become basins.
params.opening_radius: 10,10,10 voxels of binary opening detach thin bridges between objects before the distance map.
params.closing_radius: 10,10,10 voxels of closing fill small holes inside objects.
params.distance_inside_is_positive: Off: SimpleITK's convention, inside is negative.
params.distance_squared: Off: true Euclidean distance in mm.
params.mark_watershed_line: On: dam lines between basins are drawn, which shows where touching objects were split.
params.outside_value: 0 is the background label, so the result is a label map with a single foreground label.
